comparator.name: History
comparator.sourceNotes: The official course table and the 2026–2027 degree guide identify the 180 EC full-time degree. The public course table supplies the full three-year sequence, including 12 EC of second-year and 30 EC of third-year free choice. The 12 EC thesis is separate from introductory and advanced history research and the final reading assessment. No formal track is selected.
components: Independent historical inquiry based on secondary literature.
Digital collection, structuring and analysis of historical sources.
Verdiepingsvak II: concepten in de geschiedenis
Genuinely free elective space, including an optional minor or exchange.

core: Global and European historical periods, political and social change
Historical research, source criticism, historiography and independent thesis
Historical connections to contemporary societies, politics and international relations
adjacent: Material culture, archaeology, art and heritage as historical evidence
Public history, memory and communicating the past across media
questions: How do different sources and public narratives change our understanding of the past?

alternatives.label: Historical change, sources and cultures
alternatives.concept: Study historical change through empires, gender, politics, art and material culture. Develop source criticism and historical argument through literary, visual and historical evidence and a research seminar.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed schedule combines all six UCR History courses with archaeology, art history, historically situated literature, politics and source interpretation.
progression: History and art-history introductions precede advanced seminar, museums and heritage where feasible; all six term offerings, formal prerequisites, 24 unique courses, four per term and eight 300-level courses were checked against the current enriched workbook.

alternatives.label: History, heritage and public memory
alternatives.concept: Study how museums, media and communities interpret the past. Combine historical inquiry with archaeology, heritage, documentary production and public communication.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed schedule retains the history and heritage core and adds documentary, media, race and community rhetoric as substantive public-history practice.
alternatives.distinctness: 6 courses and 45 EC differ in each direction. The second option emphasises community communication, film, public memory and museum interpretation, while the first adds literary, art-historical and political inquiry.
progression: History, art history and media foundations precede work in qualitative inquiry, community communication and documentary production. Advanced heritage, media and historical research build on these foundations. Current offerings and prerequisites pass.

candidates.label: Heritage and public history across museums and media
candidates.rationale: The official public-debates module, multi-audience historical communication, and described opportunities across museums and media support the direction without constituting a named degree track.

candidates.label: Ancient and medieval historical specialization
candidates.rationale: World Archaeology, Greek Archaeology and Heritage & Ancient Democracy offer a genuine antiquity cluster, but a separate period-specialist curriculum would lack sustained medieval history, ancient or medieval source languages and period-specific research progression.

selection.assessment: The broad historical option and the heritage and public-memory option are coherent and differ by at least 30 EC. The period-specialist direction has too little sustained ancient and medieval historical progression in available course content to form a coherent third option.

blocks: Both survey modern historical change. UCR examines political, social and cultural developments from 1815.
Both examine historical change across regions. UCR focuses on empires and how historians explain their power and institutions.
Both examine early modern cross-cultural change. UCR focuses on Renaissance art and exchange around the Mediterranean.
Both examine classical Greek society. UCR focuses on the material evidence of early democracy, while UvA covers Greek and Roman antiquity more broadly.

notes.text: UvA combines broad historical study with dedicated work in digital sources, historical theory, primary-source research and a required thesis. UCR combines history with archaeology, art history and media. The options give different ways to study the past and how it is presented.

audience.programmeDescription: History at the University of Amsterdam covers historical periods, historiography and the study of primary sources. Students develop independent research through seminars and a thesis, with room for electives.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines history with art, archaeology, literature and politics. The second focuses on how museums, media and communities interpret the past.
